input.question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?
input.ground_truth: There are development languages that are cross platform. This is one way this can be accomplished. The same code base will run in various environments (Linux/BSD/Windows) and then OS specific code can be ran inside the software that is called based on what environment the code detects. Also, a second way would be runtime emulation such as WINE, but I don't think that is what you are referring to

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do the same programs run on different operating systems?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy car, and you want to play with it in your room and also in your friend’s room. Your room and your friend’s room are like two different operating systems (like Windows and Mac). 

Now, the toy car is like a program (like a game or a drawing app). But your toy car doesn’t drive by itself in every room. You need to have a special set of instructions or a “remote control” that works in both rooms.

Sometimes, the toy car comes with two different remotes—one for your room and one for your friend’s room. That’s like having two versions of the program, one for each operating system.

But sometimes, the toy car is very smart! It has a special adapter (called a “virtual machine” or “cross-platform” code) that lets you use the same remote in both rooms. Or, someone made a new remote that works in both rooms by understanding how both rooms work.

So, the same program can run on different operating systems because smart people make sure the program knows how to work with different “rooms” (operating systems), either by having special versions or by using clever tricks!
